correctness.rationale: For each path the homogeneous closed-neighborhood recurrence has period three; the endpoint conditions and the two hub equations reduce the full kernel to two free hub variables or a single relation among free residue-zero path variables. Their complete case split proves the stated exact nullities, including two-path cycles and every parity boundary. The all-ones press is a particular all-on solution because all degrees are even, giving exactly 2^nullity solutions. An independently implemented row-reduction verifier checks 12,074 labelled ordered length vectors, a separate recurrence checks matching parity on 139 instances, and full binary-pattern enumeration checks 41 small graphs. Finite tests are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The complete period-three path/terminal reduction determines the F2 nullity and all-on solution count on every Eulerian generalized-theta graph, including arbitrarily high nullities. Codsi et al. provide only a general determinant/odd-matching test for uniqueness; Dolati and Golalizadeh give a total matching count on the same graph family which, together with Codsi et al., can recover uniqueness alone. These older claims do not supply positive nullity dimensions. Ballard et al. give nullity formulas for one-vertex joins, not two-terminal multitheta junctions. An inaccessible full text and differently indexed equivalences remain real priority risks.
residual_risks: The complete Dolati–Golalizadeh 2012 primary PDF could not be read, despite finding indexed Lemma 8; it is directly relevant for matching parity and may contain further formulas not visible in accessible excerpts.

Other unindexed literature may state the binary adjacency-plus-identity nullity under graph-amalgamation terminology; unsuccessful searches do not establish global novelty.

value.rationale: The exact F2 kernel dimension of the closed-neighborhood matrix, not merely invertibility, is a natural linear-algebraic invariant governing how many winning press sets the Lights Out game admits. The recent extremality work and the earlier generalized-theta matching count provide only a binary parity decision, leaving positive nullities unresolved. The sharp residue classification gives every solution multiplicity throughout the entire even-path 2-connected Eulerian family, including arbitrarily high nullities, and structural examples with divisible-by-three cycles despite unique pressing. This resolves a motivated graph-family problem beyond a finite parameter census.
